_meta.purpose: Pre-resolved registry values for downstream agents. Agents consuming this file do NOT need to load raw registry files.

spec_identity.notes: Sixth interior RP spec (after SF_DRYWALL_WALL_INT_RP, SF_DRYWALL_CEILING_INT_RP, SF_TRIM_INT_RP, SF_DOOR_INT_RP, SF_WINDOW_INT_RP). Combined prime + finish for interior stair system repaint. Consolidates two NC specs: SF_STAIR_RISER_NC (30 tasks, risers/stringers) + SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC (43 tasks, balusters/newels/handrails/base rails) = 73 NC tasks into projected 60 RP tasks. Context prefix STRP (STair RePaint) confirmed collision-free. TSK_STRS_* is NC riser/stringer; TSK_STRL_* is NC railing. TSK_WLRP_* is wall RP; TSK_CLRP_* is ceiling RP; TSK_TMRP_* is trim RP; TSK_DIRP_* is door RP; TSK_WNRP_* is window RP. STRP avoids all collisions. Verified: zero TSK_STRP_* IDs exist in id_registry.json context_prefixes_in_use.

paintable_items.name: Stair riser face
paintable_items.notes: Reuse existing item from SF_STAIR_RISER_NC. Same physical item in RP context. EA counting from PaintScope geometry system. Riser SF per unit ~2.2 SF.

paintable_items.name: Stringer / skirtboard
paintable_items.notes: Reuse existing item from SF_STAIR_RISER_NC. Same physical item in RP context. LF from geometry system rake_length. Open/closed stringer_type modifier applies.

paintable_items.name: Baluster / spindle
paintable_items.notes: Used in SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC spec.json paintable_items but NOT registered in id_registry.json. Proposing formal registration. EA counting. Profile type (square/turned) drives 1.75x modifier. Highest per-unit labor density of any stairway component.

paintable_items.name: Newel post
paintable_items.notes: Used in SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC spec.json paintable_items but NOT registered in id_registry.json. Proposing formal registration. EA counting. Typically 2-4 per flight. Larger than balusters with decorative detail.

paintable_items.name: Handrail
paintable_items.notes: Used in SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC spec.json paintable_items but NOT registered in id_registry.json. Proposing formal registration. LF counting. 4 paintable surfaces. Optional poly topcoat at QT5. QT4+ bracket removal.

paintable_items.name: Base rail / shoe rail
paintable_items.notes: Used in SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC spec.json paintable_items but NOT registered in id_registry.json. Proposing formal registration. LF counting. Conditional — not all railing systems have base rails.

task_prefix.collision_check: No collision. TSK_STRS_* is NC riser/stringer (SF_STAIR_RISER_NC, 30 tasks). TSK_STRL_* is NC railing (SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC, 43 tasks). TSK_WLRP_* is wall RP. TSK_CLRP_* is ceiling RP. TSK_TMRP_* is trim RP. TSK_DIRP_* is door RP. TSK_WNRP_* is window RP. TSK_STRP_* is unique for interior stair RP. Checked against id_registry.json context_prefixes_in_use — STRP not present.
task_prefix.naming_rule: TSK_STRP_{ACTION} — action should be verb-based (ASSESS_CONDITION, ASSESS_ADHESION, ASSESS_COATING_ID, ASSESS_ANTISLIP, DEGLOSS_RISER, DEGLOSS_STRINGER, DEGLOSS_BALUSTER, DEGLOSS_NEWEL, DEGLOSS_HANDRAIL, DEGLOSS_BASE_RAIL, SCRAPE_FEATHER_RISER_STRINGER, SCRAPE_FEATHER_RAILING, TSP_WASH, PRIME_STRINGER, PRIME_RISER, PRIME_BALUSTER, PRIME_NEWEL, PRIME_HANDRAIL, PRIME_BASE_RAIL, BRUSH_FINISH_STRINGER, BRUSH_FINISH_RISER, BRUSH_FINISH_BALUSTER, etc.). ALL tasks in this combined RP spec use the STRP_ prefix — both RP-new tasks and tasks adapted from NC riser/railing specs. Direct NC task transfers are re-issued under TSK_STRP_* for prefix consistency.

expected_modules.notes: Tread protection (Ram Board Stair Armor, FIRST task), floor protection at landings, wall masking (spray or brush near finished walls), spray containment (spray only), carpet runner protection (if present), safety signage for occupied home. Method-dependent protection scope.

RP-specific: condition inspection of all stair components, adhesion test (ASTM D3359), coating identification (latex vs alkyd solvent test), anti-slip verification. Assessment maps to 'prep' phase — no 'assessment' phase value exists in controlled_enums. FIXED time tasks. Must fire BEFORE any prep work.

TSP wash (all components), degloss per component type (riser EA, stringer LF, baluster EA, newel EA, handrail LF, base rail LF), scrape/feather (condition-gated: FAIR/POOR only, separate tasks for riser/stringer vs railing components), caulk assess/replace (stringer-to-wall, riser-to-stringer, newel junctions — partial replacement not full re-caulk), dust removal. Canonical painting sequence within module: stringers -> risers -> balusters -> newels -> handrails -> base rails.

State-driven primer: SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT (alkyd existing or adhesion failure), SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT (smoke/nicotine damage — shellac BIN), SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT (moisture damage with mildew history). Conditional on substrate_state. Separate prime tasks per component type following canonical sequence. No primer for SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT with good adhesion test + latex existing.

Fine-finish interstage protocol at all tiers: inspect coat, light sand between coats (QT3 spot 220, QT4 full 220, QT5 thorough 220-320), patch/repair defects, spot coat patched areas, tack clean. Runs between each coat pair. Universal for stairs — scrutinized surface. Consolidated from duplicate NC riser + railing interstage modules.

Finish coat application — brush or spray. Separate tasks per component type following canonical sequence: stringers -> risers -> balusters -> newels -> handrails -> base rails. 2 coats standard (QT3-QT4), 3 coats QT5 brush per FFD 15.10.3. Fine-finish coating systems: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (QT3), SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE (QT4), SYS_FF_PREMIUM (QT5). Optional poly topcoat on handrails at QT5. Bracket removal/reinstall at QT4+. Feel test on handrails at QT5.

Final inspection (all components), touch-up, protection teardown (wall mask, spray containment, carpet protection, floor protection), tread protection removal (LAST task — may be deferred if tread work follows), customer walkthrough (RP-specific), tool cleanup. Consolidated from duplicate NC riser + railing cleanup modules.

Shared lead-safe RRP module. Conditional on PS_META.BOOL.HOME_PRE_1978. Shared across all interior RP specs. Pre-existing shared module — not owned by this spec. Stair components are HIGH RISK for lead paint — historically oil-based, typically multi-layer from multiple repaints.

Total LF of stringer/skirtboard runs. From geometry system rake_length.
Count of balusters/spindles to be repainted. Typical: 39-62+ per flight.
paintscope_keys.notes: Used in SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC but not yet registered as a PS key in id_registry.

paintscope_keys.description: Count of newel posts to be repainted. Typically 2-4 per flight.
paintscope_keys.notes: Used in SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC but not yet registered as a PS key in id_registry.

paintscope_keys.description: Total LF of handrail runs. 4 paintable surfaces per LF.
paintscope_keys.notes: Used in SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC but not yet registered as a PS key in id_registry.

paintscope_keys.description: Total LF of base rail / shoe rail. Conditional — not all systems have base rails.
paintscope_keys.notes: Used in SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC but not yet registered as a PS key in id_registry.

paintscope_keys.description: Stringer-to-wall caulk joint LF. In RP, assess & replace failed sections only (15-30% typically).
Tread protection area. Mandatory from Day 1. Ram Board Stair Armor.
Landing floor protection area at top and bottom of stairway.
Wall masking LF along stringer edge and railing area for spray method. Also needed for brush near finished walls.
Surface condition enum (GOOD/FAIR/POOR) for condition modifier selection. Values from condition_scale enum.
paintscope_keys.notes: Shared with SF_DRYWALL_WALL_INT_RP and SF_DOOR_INT_RP (proposed there first). RP-specific condition assessment driving prep intensity.

paintscope_keys.description: Interior substrate state classification (SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT through SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE). Drives primer selection logic.
paintscope_keys.notes: Shared with SF_DRYWALL_WALL_INT_RP and SF_DOOR_INT_RP (proposed there first).

paintscope_keys.description: Boolean flag indicating home built before 1978, triggering RRP lead-safe module.
paintscope_keys.notes: Shared with other interior RP specs (proposed in wall RP first). Stairs are HIGH RISK for lead paint.

paintscope_keys.description: Contamination type: none, mildew, smoke, water_stain. Drives primer selection and treatment task activation.
paintscope_keys.notes: Shared with other interior RP specs (proposed in wall RP first).

paintscope_keys.description: Baluster profile type (square/turned) driving 1.75x complexity modifier on baluster tasks.
paintscope_keys.notes: Configuration dimension from NC railing spec. Values: square, turned.

paintscope_keys.description: Stringer type (open/closed) driving 1.4x rate modifier on stringer tasks.
paintscope_keys.notes: Configuration dimension from NC riser spec. Values: open, closed.

paintscope_keys.description: Stairwell access method driving access modifier on stringer tasks. Values: step_ladder (1.3x), extension_ladder (1.6x), scaffolding (2.0x), lift (2.5x), tall_lift (2.8x).
paintscope_keys.notes: From PaintScope Stairwell Geometry System. Standard residential stairwells are step_ladder (<=12 ft).

paintscope_keys.description: Room count — drives per-room heuristics (customer walkthrough fixed-time tasks).

quality_tier.notes: QT2 excluded per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 10.1 — stairs are scrutinized, prominent surfaces requiring minimum QT3. QT modifiers: QT3=1.0x, QT4=1.3x, QT5=1.5x.

application_method.notes: Brush is default for stair detail work. Spray for large-scope production (20+ balusters break-even). HVLP preferred over airless for in-place baluster work per doctrine 6.3. In occupied RP homes, brush is even more dominant due to containment difficulty.

sheen.notes: Semi-gloss is default for stairs (scuff/hand-oil resistance). Satin at QT3+. Semi-gloss at QT4+. Gloss at QT5 only. Flat/matte/eggshell NOT valid for stairs per doctrine.

phase.notes: Assessment tasks map to 'prep' phase — no 'assessment' phase value exists in controlled_enums. 'apply' omitted from values because spec uses prime/finish directly.

unit_of_measure.notes: EA for riser, baluster, newel tasks and per-stairway-system tasks. LF for stringer, handrail, base rail tasks. SF for protection area. EA_ROOM for per-room heuristics. FIXED for assessment and customer walkthrough.

substrate_state.notes: All 5 interior RP substrate states accepted. Output normalizes to standard SS_PAINTED_* per selected sheen. Different stair components may have different substrate states (e.g., handrails FAIR/high wear, risers GOOD/low touch). Assessment determines per-component condition.

condition_scale.notes: Universal 3-level condition scale per controlled_enums.json. Drives prep pool modifier: GOOD=1.0x, FAIR=1.5x, POOR=2.0x.

consumable_category.notes: All categories valid for stair RP. 'tool' covers assessment kit, contour scrapers. 'prep' covers TSP, deglosser, flow additive.

product_role.notes: Primer = state-driven RP primers. Finish = fine-finish QT-driven systems. Clear = optional poly topcoat on handrails. Specialty = shellac stain blocker, biocide.

yield_uom.notes: EA for per-item consumables (balusters, newels, risers). LF for linear consumables (handrails, stringers, base rails). SF for coverage-based consumables. GAL for product yield.

protection_level.notes: full_cover for stair_tread_covers (mandatory Stair Armor). edge_only for floor_perimeter (canvas drops at landings). light_mask for wall_adjacent (brush near finished walls). full_mask for spray_containment (spray method). full_cover for carpet_runner_protection (rosin paper).

floor_type.notes: RP almost always has finished floors at landings. Subfloor rare in occupied RP context.

modifier_mechanism.notes: QT3=baseline (1.0x), QT4=selective_multiplier (1.3x on qt_scaled tasks), QT5=selective_multiplier (1.5x) + additional_rounds (coat 3 brush per FFD 15.10.3).

surface_ids.primary_surface_note: stair_riser is representative for riser component. Six primary surfaces in this consolidated spec: stair_riser, stair_stringer, stair_baluster, stair_newel, stair_handrail, stair_base_rail. stair_riser and stair_stringer are existing. stair_baluster, stair_newel, stair_handrail, stair_base_rail need to be proposed.
surface_ids.notes: stair_riser, stair_stringer, stair_tread are existing in id_registry.json surface_ids entries_in_active_use. stair_baluster, stair_newel, stair_handrail, stair_base_rail are used in SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC spec.json but NOT in entries_in_active_use — proposing addition. wall_field: stairwell wall adjacent to stringer. trim_baseboard: landing baseboard (handled by SF_TRIM_INT_RP).

zone_ids.notes: Ram Board Stair Armor mandatory from Day 1. NEVER plastic sheeting (fall hazard). FIRST setup task, LAST teardown task. In RP occupied context, daily verification of integrity required.
Canvas drop cloth runners at landing floors (top and bottom of stairway). Almost always needed in RP (finished floors).
Wall masking along stringer edge and railing area. Required for spray method. In RP, may also be needed for brush method near finished walls at stringer-to-wall junction.

Cardboard shields behind balusters, Tape & Drape on walls. Spray method only. HVLP preferred over airless for in-place baluster work. 45+ min setup for typical 39-62 baluster system. Not currently in id_registry zone_ids entries_in_active_use.
RP-specific: occupied homes may have carpet runner on stairs. Rosin paper over carpet edges at paint work zones. Not present in NC (carpet installed after painting). New zone not in id_registry.

material_system_prefix.notes: All 7 material systems are existing/shared. Three RP primer systems (adhesion, stain-block, mildew) are shared with wall RP, door RP, trim RP, and other interior RP specs (proposed in SF_DRYWALL_WALL_INT_RP resolution). Three fine-finish systems (QT3/QT4/QT5) are shared with NC stair, NC trim, NC door, and all other fine-finish specs. SYS_TOPCOAT_POLY_HANDRAIL is from NC railing spec — optional QT5 poly topcoat on handrails for hand-oil resistance. No new material systems needed for this spec.

shared_rp_consumables.name: Liquid Sander / Deglosser
shared_rp_consumables.notes: RP-specific. Proposed in SF_TRIM_INT_RP resolution. Chemical degloss for existing paint — faster than mechanical on complex profiles (turned balusters), no sanding dust. Shared across interior RP specs.

shared_rp_consumables.name: RP Assessment Kit (Adhesion + Coating ID)
shared_rp_consumables.notes: RP-specific. Proposed in SF_TRIM_INT_RP resolution. Cross-hatch cutter, tape (ASTM D3359), mineral spirits, white rags. Shared across interior RP specs.

shared_rp_consumables.name: TSP (Trisodium Phosphate) Cleaner
shared_rp_consumables.notes: RP-specific surface decontamination wash. Proposed in SF_DOOR_INT_RP resolution. Removes hand oils, cleaning chemical residue. Shared across interior RP specs.

proposed_consumables.name: German Round Trim Brush (1.25 inch)
proposed_consumables.justification: For turned baluster profile work. Avoids roping on complex curves. Transfers from NC railing spec. Reusable across stair RP projects.

proposed_consumables.name: Flow Additive (Floetrol for latex / Penetrol for alkyd)
proposed_consumables.justification: Extends open time and improves leveling on turned balusters and handrails. Prevents roping on complex profiles. Transfers from NC railing spec.

proposed_consumables.name: Tape & Drape Film (pre-taped masking film)
proposed_consumables.justification: For spray containment on walls adjacent to railing system. Faster application than separate tape + plastic sheeting.

proposed_consumables.name: Safe-Release Masking Tape (low tack)
proposed_consumables.justification: For tread protection attachment and carpet runner protection where standard blue tape may damage finished treads or carpet backing. Low-tack adhesive.

proposed_rounds.description: State-driven prime + 2 finish coats. Standard RP sequence for FAIR/POOR condition stair components requiring primer.
proposed_rounds.notes: Most common RP round for stairs with adhesion or contamination issues. Prime coat is state-driven (adhesion, stain-block, or mildew primer). All 6 component types follow same round.

proposed_rounds.description: 2 finish coats only. GOOD condition, no prime needed — sound paint with adhesion verified.
proposed_rounds.notes: Skip prime when adhesion test passes, existing paint is sound, and coating is compatible (latex over latex). Most common residential stair repaint scenario.

proposed_rounds.description: Prime + 3 finish coats. QT5 + brush per FFD 15.10.3 + FAIR/POOR condition.
proposed_rounds.notes: Maximum coat sequence for stairs. State-driven prime + 3 brush finish coats with thorough interstage at 220-320 grit.

proposed_rounds.description: 3 finish coats. QT5 + brush + GOOD condition.
proposed_rounds.notes: QT5 brush adds 3rd finish coat per FFD 15.10.3 even without prime.

proposed_profiles.description: Coverage rate for adhesion primer on previously painted stair component surfaces. Different absorption than bare-wood primer.
proposed_profiles.notes: Previously painted surfaces absorb less primer than bare wood. Expected coverage varies by component: risers ~2.2 SF/EA, stringers ~1 SF/LF, balusters square ~1.5-2.0 SF/EA, balusters turned ~2.0-3.0 SF/EA, newels ~4-8 SF/EA, handrails ~1.75 SF/LF.

proposed_profiles.description: Coverage rate for shellac stain blocker on smoke-damaged stair surfaces.
proposed_profiles.notes: Shellac primers have lower coverage than latex. Expect 250-350 SF-equivalent/gal.

proposed_profiles.description: Coverage rate for fine-finish enamel on repainted stair component surfaces.
proposed_profiles.notes: Similar to NC fine-finish coverage but slightly better absorption on previously painted substrate. Coverage rates per component transfer from NC specs. Materials Manager to evaluate if COV_STRS_FINISH can be reused.

existing_modifiers_to_reuse.notes: Shared per RP convention. Drives prep pool: GOOD=1.0x, FAIR=1.5x, POOR=2.0x. Proposed in wall/door RP resolutions.
Shared per RP convention. Drives treatment task activation and primer selection. Proposed in wall/door RP resolutions.

existing_modifiers_from_nc.notes: Transfers from NC railing spec unchanged. Square=1.0x, turned=1.75x per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 9.2. Applies to ALL baluster-specific tasks: degloss, scrape/feather, prime, finish coat. Does NOT apply to newel, handrail, base rail, riser, or stringer tasks.
Transfers from NC riser spec unchanged. Closed=1.0x, open=1.4x (midpoint of 1.3-1.5x range). Applies to ALL stringer tasks: degloss, scrape/feather, prime, finish, interstage sanding.

Transfers from NC riser spec unchanged. Applies to stringer tasks based on max working height: step_ladder (<=12 ft)=1.3x, extension_ladder (<=18 ft)=1.6x, scaffolding (<=24 ft)=2.0x, lift (<=28 ft)=2.5x, tall_lift (>28 ft)=2.8x. Standard residential is step_ladder. Applies ALONE — does NOT stack with standard height modifiers. All other components (risers, balusters, newels, handrails) are H1_STANDARD (1.0x).

prep_pool.formula: condition_modifier x component_modifier (one of: baluster_profile, stringer_type+access, or 1.0x for riser/newel/handrail/base_rail)
prep_pool.max_theoretical: POOR(2.0) x turned_baluster(1.75) = 3.50x for baluster prep; POOR(2.0) x open_stringer(1.4) x scaffolding(2.0) = 5.60x for stringer prep
prep_pool.flag_note: Stringer prep max exceeds 4.0x flag. However, open stringer + POOR + scaffolding access is an extremely rare combination in residential RP. More realistic max: POOR(2.0) x open_stringer(1.4) x step_ladder(1.3) = 3.64x. Flag for estimator review if scaffolding + POOR.

coating_pool.max_theoretical: QT5(1.5) x turned_baluster(1.75) = 2.63x for baluster coating; QT5(1.5) x open_stringer(1.4) x scaffolding(2.0) = 4.20x for stringer coating
coating_pool.flag_note: Stringer coating max exceeds 4.0x flag. However, QT5 + open stringer + scaffolding is extremely rare residential. Realistic max: QT5(1.5) x open_stringer(1.4) x step_ladder(1.3) = 2.73x.

coordination_notes: Stair RP consolidates SF_STAIR_RISER_NC + SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC into a single RP spec. Canonical painting sequence (stringers -> risers -> balusters -> newels -> handrails -> base rails) becomes intra-spec ordering.

Stair RP runs alongside trim RP (SF_TRIM_INT_RP) which covers landing baseboard. Stringer connects to baseboard at landing — same finish group. Sequencing: stair components and trim in coordinated visit.
Stair RP may run alongside wall RP (SF_DRYWALL_WALL_INT_RP) for stairwell walls. Stair components first, then stairwell walls per A-005 (trim/doors before walls).
Wall masking for stair spray (wall_adjacent zone) may be already in place from wall RP spray setup — coordination avoids duplicate protection.
MOD_RRP_INT_CONTAINMENT is shared across all interior RP specs — do not duplicate lead-safe tasks. Stair components are HIGH RISK for lead paint.
Stair tread protection (stair_tread_covers zone) may be maintained if tread work (SF_STAIR_TREAD spec) follows stair component painting. Tread removal may be deferred.
Access staging overhead (15-40% per doctrine Section 5.6) is project-level overhead, not per-task. Estimator should apply as project-level multiplier, not baked into individual task rates.

cross_file_threading: RULE 1: Every TSK_ in sop_modules.json MUST have a matching rate in production.json
RULE 2: Every ITM_ in spec.json MUST appear in at least one variant
RULE 3: Every SYS_ quality_tier MUST match spec.json configuration_dimensions
RULE 4: Every IN_ input in spec.json SHOULD be consumed by sop_modules or production
RULE 5: Every PS_ key in production.json MUST match spec.json required_paintscope_inputs
RULE 6: Every zone_id in spec.json MUST match sop_modules.json protection_metadata.zones
RULE 7: Module phase order: setup -> prep -> prime -> apply -> interstage -> finish -> cleanup
RULE 8: UOM for a task MUST match between sop_modules.json and production.json
RULE 9: Every TSK_ context prefix from resolution.json MUST be used in sop_modules.json and production.json
RULE 10: Every ITM_ marked 'existing' in resolution.json MUST use the exact registered ID
RULE 11: Downstream agents MUST use only enum values from resolution.json applicable_enums
